title: DARS: Dual-Level Credit Assignment RL with Structured Reasoning for Instruction-Based Image Editing
abstract: arXiv:2608.20161v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Instruction-based image editing uses a planner-renderer pipeline: a vision-language model (VLM) first converts the instruction into an edit plan, and a diffusion model then executes that plan. Training such systems with only final-image rewards is inefficient because a poor edit does not reveal whether additional optimization should place more emphasis on the planner or the renderer, and even planner-dominant cases remain difficult to localize within a free-form reasoning trace. We present DARS, a reinforcement learning framework for dual-level credit assignment in this two-stage setting. Across modules, multi-plan multi-render rollouts estimate between-plan and within-plan reward variability for soft module routing, while rollout mean rewards provide hardness estimates for an adaptive curriculum. translated_title: DARS：基于结构化推理的双层级信用分配强化学习用于指令式图像编辑
translated_abstract: 指令式图像编辑采用规划器-渲染器流水线：视觉语言模型（VLM）首先将指令转换为编辑计划，然后扩散模型执行该计划。仅使用最终图像奖励来训练此类系统效率低下，因为一个糟糕的编辑无法揭示额外优化应更多侧重于规划器还是渲染器，即使在规划器主导的情况下，也难以在自由形式的推理轨迹中定位问题。我们提出了DARS，一种用于这种两阶段设置中双层级信用分配的强化学习框架。在模块间，多计划多渲染的 rollout 估计计划间和计划内的奖励变异性，以进行软模块路由，而 rollout 平均奖励提供难度估计用于自适应课程。在规划器内部，四字段结构化推理输出实现了前缀门控奖励和令牌级优势重加权，将输出转化为可操作的反馈信号。
tldr: 本文提出DARS框架，通过模块间软路由和规划器内结构化推理的令牌级奖励重加权，解决了指令式图像编辑中规划器与渲染器间的信用分配难题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes DARS, a reinforcement learning framework that addresses credit assignment between planner and renderer in instruction-based image editing via inter-module soft routing and intra-planner token-level reward reweighting with structured reasoning.
